title: After 31 Years, Foo Fighters Are Finally Coming to India. Tickets Drop Today at Noon.
excerpt: Dave Grohl and co. land in Bengaluru on January 29 and Mumbai on January 31 — two all-day rock spectacles that complete India's transformation into a global tour stop. Here's everything the diaspora needs to know before BookMyShow melts down.
body:
For thirty-one years, the most famous answer in rock to the question "have you ever played India?" was a sheepish no. As of this morning, that sentence is dead.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=NWU33fvPxd0</youtube>

**Foo Fighters** — Rock & Roll Hall of Famers, fifteen-time Grammy winners, the band that turned grief into stadium catharsis after Nirvana — have announced their first-ever India tour. Two dates, two cities, January 2027: **Bengaluru LIVE** on January 29, and the **Mahalaxmi Racecourse** in Mumbai on January 31. And the part you actually need to act on — general sale opens at **12 PM IST today, Tuesday, June 16, exclusively on BookMyShow**. If you have NRI relatives already texting you about it, this is why.

Dave Grohl, who has spent three decades as rock's most likeable frontman, put it the way only he could.

> "After 31 years as a band, we can't wait to FINALLY play for our fans in India!! It's taken a few years but we promise it'll be worth the wait. We hope Bengaluru and Mumbai are ready for a couple of very long, very loud nights." — Dave Grohl

Very long, very loud is not marketing fluff. These aren't standalone arena gigs — both shows are being built as **all-day rock spectacles** under the *Bandland on Tour* banner, produced and promoted by BookMyShow Live, with a genre-spanning undercard before the headliners take the stage. The Bengaluru bill stacks **Pinkshift**, **Alain Johannes**, Austin punks **Die Spitz**, and New York's **The Pretty Reckless** (yes, Taylor Momsen's band) ahead of the Foos. Mumbai gets Goa rockers **Still In Therapy** and singer-songwriter **Mali** alongside Die Spitz and The Pretty Reckless. The Mumbai gates open at 3 PM for a seven-hour day — pace yourselves.

The band that touches down won't be a nostalgia act coasting on *The Colour and the Shape*. The Foos arrive on the back of **Your Favorite Toy**, their twelfth studio album, released in April — which means the setlist will weave fresh material through the canon everyone's screaming for. And let's be honest about what that canon is. *Everlong*. *My Hero*. *Times Like These*. *Best of You*. *The Pretender*. *Learn to Fly*. These are songs that an entire generation of Indian millennials downloaded on dodgy connections, learned on first guitars, and played at every college fest from Bangalore to Bombay. There is going to be a lot of grown men crying during *Everlong*, and that is exactly the point.

The current lineup is the road-hardened one: Grohl up front, Pat Smear and Chris Shiflett on guitars, Nate Mendel on bass, Rami Jaffee on keys, and recently-inducted **Ilan Rubin** behind the kit — the seat that has carried the weight of Taylor Hawkins's absence with quiet grace.

## Why this matters beyond the mosh pit

For the diaspora, this booking is the punctuation mark on a story that's been building for years. India used to be the country world tours skipped — too logistically thorny, too unproven a market. That excuse is gone. In the span of a couple of seasons, promoters have landed **Coldplay**, **Ed Sheeran**, **Post Malone**, and **Guns N' Roses** on Indian soil, each show selling out with a ferocity that rewrote the spreadsheets. Foo Fighters slotting India into a run that also includes Pinkpop in the Netherlands and Rock in Rio in Brazil isn't a favour — it's a recognition. India is now a tour stop, full stop.

Which brings up the diaspora math everyone's quietly running. The shows land in late January — peak season for NRIs already planning winter trips home for weddings and the post-holiday lull. A Foo Fighters ticket is suddenly a very good reason to anchor that Bengaluru or Mumbai visit. Expect the BookMyShow queue at noon to be thick with VPNs from New Jersey, Toronto, and Wembley as much as Whitefield.

A word of strategy, because this will move fast: international debuts in India have a habit of selling out their good tiers within the hour (ask anyone who tried for Coldplay). If you're flying in for it, lock the ticket *before* the flight. Mahalaxmi Racecourse under a January Mumbai sky, Grohl howling into the night, fifty thousand voices on the *Best of You* outro — it'll be worth every minute of the wait Grohl kept apologising for.

Thirty-one years late. Right on time.
